sources: github.com/certik/fortran-utils (depth-1 clone): src/optimize.f90, src/ppm.f90, src/mesh.f90, src/sorting.f90

parse.errors: none reported; sample1.f is 'partial' (tool's meaning: zero symbols AND zero references)

languages.convention: modules, programs, subroutines, functions, named/generic interfaces and interface-declared procedures; not module variables or parameters
missed_examples: mesh.f90:14 function meshexp(rmin, rmax, a, N) result(mesh)
languages.pattern: The zero is real. The tags query the tool gets for fortran (inferred by gotreesitter v0.50.1, no RepoCortex supplement) contains only two @reference.call patterns ((call_expression (identifier)) and (call (identifier))) and no @definition pattern at all, so no module/subroutine/function can ever become a symbol; the grammar does produce (module_statement (name)), (subroutine_statement (name)), (function_statement (name)) nodes. Files show parse_status 'ok' only because call references were recorded.

sources: each also copied with a .fsx extension (identical content) to reach the fsharp grammar

parse.errors: as .fs: all 5 parse_status 'skipped', parse_error 'no tags query available for "forth"'; as .fsx: all 5 'partial' (zero symbols, zero references), no error text

languages.convention: named modules (top-level and nested), types (class, record, abbreviation, interface), module-level let bindings, members (member/override/static member/member val); not namespaces, constructors, class-private let bindings, val fields, record fields
missed_examples: sample.fs:12 let Sample1(xs : int list) : string =
languages.pattern: Two independent failures. (1) Every .fs file is detected as Forth, which has no tags query, so real F# source is skipped outright (phase A saw 0 fsharp files for this reason); only .fsx/.fsi reach the fsharp grammar. (2) Even then the only pattern is (type_definition (identifier) @name), which never matches because the grammar nests the name as type_definition > record_type_defn/interface_type_defn/... > type_name > identifier; there is no pattern for let bindings, modules or members.

languages.convention: func, class / class_name, signal, enum and const declarations; not script-level var/export var/onready var (36 of those exist and are also not extracted)
languages.pattern: The zero is real. The inferred query has (function_definition (identifier) @name) and (class_definition (identifier) @name), but this grammar names definitions with a (name) node, not (identifier) (e.g. (function_definition (name) (parameters) (body ...))), so the definition patterns can never match. Only call references are recorded (170 across the 4 files), which is why the files read 'ok'. 20 of the 31 expected are functions/classes; all 20 missed.

parse.errors: none reported; all 5 'partial' (zero symbols and zero references)

languages.convention: functions (pub fn, fn, external fn, @external fn), custom types and type aliases, constants; not type constructors/variants
missed_examples: pair.gleam:9 pub fn first(pair: #(a, b)) -> a {
io.gleam:14 pub fn print(string: String) -> Nil
websocket.gleam:44 pub external fn receive(from: Connection, within: Int) -> ...
languages.pattern: The zero is real. The inferred query has three type patterns and no function pattern: functions are (function (visibility_modifier) (identifier) ...) nodes that no pattern mentions, and the type patterns expect type_definition > type_identifier directly while the grammar produces type_definition > type_name > type_identifier, so they never match either. No reference patterns exist, hence 'partial'. The older Linguist samples (contributor.gleam, websocket.gleam, pre-1.0 syntax) also produce ERROR nodes, but the modern stdlib files fail identically.

languages.convention: function definitions (with a body), structs, named uniform/buffer interface blocks, and global uniform/in/out/varying variables; not prototypes, struct members or locals
missed_examples: SyLens.glsl:17 uniform float kCoeff, kCube, uShift, vShift;
closesthit_rchit.glsl:17 layout(binding = 2, set = 0) uniform UBO { ... } ubo;
languages.pattern: Every function definition (31 of 31) and every struct (3 of 3, reported as kind 'class') is extracted at the right line with no false positives; prototypes are correctly not reported. All 28 misses are the shader interface: global uniforms/varyings/in/out variables and uniform/buffer blocks have no pattern. Counting functions and structs only, recall is 34/34.
languages.detection_notes: Unrenamed Linguist files: .vs .fp .tesc .rchit .fsh .glslf are detected as glsl; extrude_normals.gs is detected as javascript and recurse1.fs as forth (skipped, no tags query).

languages.convention: build-configuration language: counted named targets (group/config/source_set/pkg_config/shim_headers("name")), template("name") definitions and declare_args() build arguments; not plain assignments inside targets
languages.pattern: The zero is real. The inferred query is a single reference pattern, (call_expression (identifier) @name) @reference.call, so a target such as group("icu") is stored as a call reference to 'group' (27 references over the 4 files) and nothing is ever a definition. Target names are string literals, which the query never captures.

languages.convention: type-system definitions (type, interface, union, enum, scalar, input, directive) plus named operations (query/mutation/subscription) and fragments; not fields, arguments, enum values (accepted as correct when extracted) or 'extend type'
wrong_examples: schema_graphqls.graphql:30 symbol with an EMPTY name, kind 'function' (from the empty-bodied 'enum PriceAdjustmentCodesEnum @doc(...) { }')
missed_examples: kitchen-sink.graphql:8 query queryName($foo: ComplexType, $site: Site = MOBILE) {
languages.pattern: Schema (SDL) files are extracted completely: all 56 type/interface/union/enum/scalar/input/directive definitions found, plus 7 enum values. Client documents are invisible: named queries, mutations, subscriptions and fragments have no pattern, so an operations-only file yields nothing. Kinds are coarse: scalars, directives and enum values are labelled 'function' (10 symbols); unions, enums and inputs are labelled 'class'. An enum with an empty body yields one empty-named symbol.
languages.detection_notes: .graphqls is detected as graphql without renaming (same symbols).

parse.errors: none reported (the grammar does emit ERROR nodes, e.g. on every 'implements' clause, but the tool does not surface them)

languages.convention: classes (incl. nested), methods, constructors, script-level def functions; not fields/properties or script variables
wrong_examples: DockerMock.groovy:4 class 'erializable' (real: class DockerMock implements Serializable)
DockerMock.groovy:30 class 'erializable' (real: class Container implements Serializable)
DockerMock.groovy:44 class 'erializable' (real: class Image implements Serializable)
DataDrivenSpec.groovy:19 class 'Specification' (the superclass in 'class DataDrivenSpec extends Specification')
missed_examples: DockerMock.groovy:23 private <T> T intercept(T instance) {  (generic method)
DataDrivenSpec.groovy:20 def "maximum of two numbers"() {  (Spock string-named method)
languages.pattern: Plain classes and ordinary methods are extracted well (all 36 ordinary methods/functions found; methods are labelled 'function'). The class pattern captures every identifier child of class_definition: 'extends X' adds the superclass as a second class symbol, and 'implements X' (which the grammar parses as an ERROR) replaces the class name with a mangled 'erializable'. Constructors, generic methods (<T> T name(...)) and Spock string-named methods are never extracted. A synthetic probe also showed enum, trait and interface-method declarations produce no symbols.
languages.detection_notes: Jenkinsfile (by filename) and .gvy are detected as groovy; template.gtpl is also parsed as groovy.

The bigger problem is detection: .hh is routed to C++, so the legacy-but-common Hack extension yields garbage (on the 6 unrenamed .hh files: 37 expected, 2 extracted, 1 correct, 1 wrong 'if'); only .hack and .hhi reach the hack grammar, and Hack-in-.php goes to php.

wrong_examples: iter.ha:51 function 'iterator' -- the return type in 'fn iter(fmt: str, args: []field) iterator = iterator {'
types.ha:165 function 'dirent' -- the return type in 'export fn dirent_dup(e: *dirent) dirent = {'

All 13 functions are found, but no type declaration is ever extracted (40 of 40 missed, and types.ha is almost entirely types). sources: github.com/HaxeFoundation/hscript (depth-1 clone): hscript/Colorizer.hx, hscript/Tools.hx, hscript/Expr.hx, hscript/Live.hx, script/RunScript.hx
Linguist has no Haxe sample folder in this checkout

parse.errors: none reported, but the grammar emits many ERROR nodes (RunScript 16, Colorizer 29, Tools 48, Expr 153) that the tool does not surface

languages.convention: classes, interfaces, enums, typedefs, methods and constructors (function new); not member vars, enum constructors or locals; both branches of #if/#else counted
missed_examples: Expr.hx:74 typedef Argument = { name : String, ?t : CType, ?opt : Bool, ?value : Expr };
Tools.hx:27 public static function iter( e : Expr, f : Expr -> Void ) {
languages.pattern: What is extracted is right (14/14), but two thirds of the definitions are lost. There is no pattern for enum, typedef or abstract (Expr.hx: 22 definitions of which 19 are enums/typedefs, 0 extracted), 'function new' has no identifier to capture, and the grammar fails on ordinary Haxe (switch/case patterns, #if blocks, try/catch), wrapping whole classes in ERROR nodes so the class itself and any method inside the broken region vanish (4 of 5 classes and 6 of 18 named methods missed).

languages.convention: configuration language: labelled top-level blocks are the definitions (resource, data, variable, output, module, provider, template; named by their last label) plus each name assigned inside a locals block; unlabelled blocks (terraform, locals), nested blocks (ingress, tags, provisioner ...) and attribute assignments are not definitions
wrong_examples: main.tf:5 function 'ingress' (nested block inside a resource)
main.tf:1 function 'elb_sec_group' duplicating deployment_unit 'elb_sec_group' on the same line
terraform.tfvars:7 function 'config' (nested block inside an attribute map)
missed_examples: example.tofu:68 full_tag_map = merge(...)  (the local value defined inside locals { })
languages.pattern: Every block at every nesting depth becomes a symbol of kind 'function', named by its last label or, when unlabelled, by its block keyword. So all 21 labelled top-level blocks are found (recall 21/22), but 23 of 52 symbols are nested or unlabelled blocks (ingress, egress, tags, terraform, locals ...). In .tf files each resource is additionally stored a second time as a 'deployment_unit' (8 duplicates); .tofu files do not get that. Resource type is not part of the name (aws_instance.example and a variable named example would collide). If every block is accepted as a definition, precision is 44/52 = 0.846.

notes: Binary under test: scratchpad/langs/repocortex. All indexing was done on copies under scratchpad/langs/work/G3/<language>/; the repository was not modified.

None of the 12 languages has a RepoCortex supplement; every tags query here is the one gotreesitter v0.50.1 infers (grammars.ResolveTagsQuery). The queries were dumped with a throwaway Go program (work/G3/scripts/dumpq) and trees with work/G3/scripts/sexp to explain each failure.

'has a tags query' does not mean 'has definition patterns': fortran and gn have reference patterns only; gdscript, gleam and fsharp have definition patterns that cannot match the grammar's actual node shapes. All five extract 0 symbols on real code.

parse_status is not a syntax-health signal for these languages: 'partial' means the file yielded zero symbols and zero references, and 'ok' means it yielded at least one of either. Files with dozens of tree-sitter ERROR nodes (Haxe, Groovy, old Gleam) are reported 'ok' or 'partial' with parse_error NULL; fortran/gdscript/gn files read 'ok' with 0 symbols because call references were recorded.
Extension routing losses: .fs -> forth (F# and GLSL fragment shaders skipped, 'no tags query available for "forth"'), .hh -> cpp (Hack parsed as C++), .gs -> javascript (GLSL geometry shaders).

Kind vocabulary is coarse: methods are 'function' in groovy/haxe (but 'method' in hack), structs/enums/unions/inputs are 'class', and any definition kind the tool does not know (graphql scalar/directive/enum value, every hcl block) falls back to 'function'. wrong_kind counts only the clearly misleading cases (function for a non-callable).

Precision is null where nothing was extracted (0/0). Enum values, struct/record fields and member variables were excluded from 'expected' in every language; where the tool extracted enum values (graphql) they were scored correct.
Nothing crashed, hung or was slow: every index run finished in under 0.4 s.
